Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: World Bank indicates government revenue and payments processes remain largely manual and there is no government payments digitization strategy; it does not describe a functioning national digital revenue collection program ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). Muni Dinero supports bill payments (e.g., SEGESA electricity), but that is not government tax revenue ([Google Play – Muni Dinero](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.munidinero.subscriber.prod&hl=en_US)).
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check (fast path, as originally scored 0 with no source) surfaced an authoritative government-linked source (Revista Real Equatorial Guinea, reporting a Treasury Ministry announcement, Nov 2025) describing an active Phase II rollout of electronic card payment for tax obligations, plus Presidential Order 3/2025 banning cash payment of public revenue (hosted on the ruling party's site, which reproduces the official order text). This substantive development was missed by the prior Unknown/no-source score, so the row was moved to the full verification path. Revised from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Partial), reflecting the pilot's limited geographic scope (Treasury windows in Malabo, following a trial at OFIVEGE) and its phased, not-yet-nationwide, extension plan as of late 2025.
revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea's Treasury and State Patrimony Department is rolling out Phase II of an electronic tax payment system, enabling citizens and businesses to pay tax obligations by debit or credit card (including via Ecobank) rather than in cash. Presidential Order 3/2025 prohibits cash payment of taxes, fees and other public revenue, requiring payment through official bank accounts or authorised electronic platforms. As of late 2025, the electronic card payment system was being piloted at Treasury windows in Malabo, following a successful trial at OFIVEGE, with a planned gradual rollout to other revenue collection points nationwide. Coverage is therefore partial rather than comprehensive.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No publicly accessible payment-scheme rulebook for Equatorial Guinea’s domestic e-money scheme or CEMAC retail instant rules was located in available sources; BEAC site references ISO 20022 adoption and circulars but not a public scheme rulebook for end users/participants ([BEAC – Accueil](https://www.beac.int/)). After searching for “rulebook”, “scheme rules”, and “GIMACPay rules”, I found only general references, not full published rules.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check (fast path, as originally scored 0 with no source) surfaced the AfricaNenda State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) 2023 CEMAC case study, co-published with the World Bank Group, which states explicitly that GIMACPAY's scheme rules 'are not publicly available'. This is a direct, authoritative answer to the variable, so the row was moved from the fast-path Unknown check to the full verification path. Revised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (No - Confidential).
revised_comments: GIMACPAY, the CEMAC regional instant payment scheme in which Equatorial Guinea participates, operates under a governance manual and scheme rules maintained by GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire et Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale), covering participant obligations, service availability, incident response and penalties for service failure. According to AfricaNenda's State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) 2023 CEMAC case study, these scheme rules are not publicly available; participants instead sign membership agreements directly with GIMAC and BEAC rather than accessing a published rulebook.
